record.original_question: Construct, in ZFC and without extra set-theoretic hypotheses, general topological spaces, and also Lindelöf topological spaces, that witness non-implications among the classical selection properties shown in the paper's classification diagrams.

evidence.quote: Project 5.2 ([24, Problem 3]). Find, without extra hypotheses, (general) topological spaces that demonstrate non-implications among the classical properties. Do the same for Lindelöf topological spaces.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. For a topological space $X$, let $\mathcal{O}$ denote the family of open covers of $X$. Several subfamilies of $\mathcal{O}$ are standard:
- $\Omega$: the $\omega$-covers, i.e., open covers $\mathcal{U}$ such that $X\notin\mathcal{U}$ and every finite subset of $X$ is contained in some member of $\mathcal{U}$.
- $\Gamma$: the $\gamma$-covers, i.e., infinite open covers $\mathcal{U}$ such that every $x\in X$ belongs to all but finitely many members of $\mathcal{U}$.

For families $\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}$ of open covers, define the classical selection principles:
- $S_1(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})$: for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ with each $\mathcal{U}_n\in\mathcal{A}$, there exist $U_n\in\mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\{U_n:n\in\mathbb{N}\}\in\mathcal{B}$.
- $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})$: for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ with each $\mathcal{U}_n\in\mathcal{A}$, there exist finite $\mathcal{F}_n\subseteq\mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\bigcup_n\mathcal{F}_n\in\mathcal{B}$.
- $U_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})$: for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of elements of $\mathcal{A}$ (none containing a finite subcover), there exist finite $\mathcal{F}_n\subseteq\mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\{\bigcup\mathcal{F}_n:n\in\mathbb{N}\}\in\mathcal{B}$.

Restricting $\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B}$ to $\{\mathcal{O},\Omega,\Gamma\}$ gives a finite collection of selection-principle properties whose provable implications are summarized in the Scheepers diagram.

Problem. Working in ZFC alone (without any additional set-theoretic axioms such as CH, $\mathfrak{p}=\mathfrak{c}$, MA, etc.), construct topological spaces witnessing each non-implication among these classical selection properties in the Scheepers diagram. That is, for every pair $(P,Q)$ of properties in the diagram such that $P\Rightarrow Q$ is not provable, exhibit in ZFC a topological space satisfying $P$ but not $Q$.

Moreover, carry out the same construction with the additional requirement that the witnessing spaces be Lindelöf.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of completing the Scheepers diagram with absolute (ZFC) examples has seen major recent progress: Peng's "Scheepers Diagram Last Theorem" has completed all provable implications in the diagram, and ZFC constructions of separating examples (including ones using the one-point compactification of $\mathbb{N}$ and functions $\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\}$) have been found. However, fully resolving the Lindelöf version with absolute examples for every non-implication is still subject to ongoing work, so the overall problem is best described as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Selection principles and proofs from the Book
status_evidence.snippet: Recent, surprising solutions to long-standing problems on the Scheepers diagram, including Peng's Scheepers Diagram Last Theorem, completing the provable implications in the diagram.
status_evidence.claim: Major non-implication problems in the Scheepers diagram have recently been resolved in ZFC.

status_evidence.title: Selection principles in mathematics: A milestone of open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Project 5.2: Find, without extra hypotheses, topological spaces demonstrating non-implications among the classical properties; do the same for Lindelöf spaces.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of ZFC separating examples (general and Lindelöf) was posed as an open project.
